changelog.notes:
Fix: saber stops waking on blade insert when JMT_BLADE_DETECT is used with a detect pin
- Only affects the combination introduced in 1.2.0. A detect pin on its own, or JMT_BLADE_DETECT without a pin, was never affected
- With both defined, two handlers were managing gesture state: Fett263's blade detect latch, and the wrapper's own BladeID-driven one. Under FETT263_SAVE_GESTURE_OFF the second save captured a gestureon the first had already cleared, so the saved preference became off and every later insert restored gestures to off
- With a detect pin the wrapper no longer runs its own gesture handling. The pin handler already does it on the contact edge, which is earlier and more reliable. Beside a pin, JMT_BLADE_DETECT now means only what it was added to mean in 1.2.0: keep the periodic BladeID scan from choosing blade configs

Blade detect pin and BladeID scanning now work together
- Fixes a stutter on blade removal: several font reloads and a repeated font.wav instead of a single bladeout.wav. It affects sabers that have a detect pin, more than one blade entry in their blades array, and something running a periodic BladeID scan
- Cause: as a blade is withdrawn its resistance climbs through every value between seated and open, and the periodic scan samples that sweep and selects whichever blade entry is numerically nearest each time. A change between two real blade entries reads to ProffieOS as a different blade rather than a removal, so it reloads the font. Sabers with a single blade entry never show it, because the nearest entry never changes
- With a detect pin the wrapper now leaves blade selection to the pin. The pin fires at the moment the contact makes or breaks, and on removal it has already marked the reading as no-blade, so the correct entry is chosen regardless of what the ID line reads mid-sweep. The periodic scan continues to feed chassis detect and no longer moves the blade config. A manual scanid is unaffected and still re-identifies immediately
- This is automatic when JMT_CHASSIS_DETECT_RANGE is enabled, since that is the setting that requires a periodic scan to exist
- JMT_BLADE_DETECT alongside a detect pin is no longer an error. It now requests the same behavior for a pin saber that runs a BladeID scan without chassis detect, and no longer requires NO_BLADE_ID_RANGE, because the pin supplies what the range was supplying
- A detect pin on its own, with no chassis range and no JMT_BLADE_DETECT, is untouched and behaves exactly as before
- Blade insert wake, gesture restore and the favorite-reset abort are unchanged

Three fixes for BladeID-driven chassis detect
- Fixed an endless font reload on blade insertion. With JMT_CHASSIS_DETECT_RANGE enabled, inserting a blade could make the saber re-scan its font and replay font.wav on every BladeID scan, over and over. It looks and sounds like the board rebooting, but the board is fine and the serial connection never drops
- Cause: the config hold added in 1.0.22 was counting calls instead of scans. ProffieOS asks for the BladeID reading once to decide whether the blade config should change, then a second time while applying that change. The hold released on the first call and re-armed on the second, so the decision was undone before it could take effect and the same config was reloaded forever. The scan is now identified directly, so the decision survives
- This also means JMT_CHASSIS_RANGE_STABLE_COUNT now debounces the number of scans it says it does. Previously a config change in progress could advance it twice in one scan, making chassis detect briefly more twitchy than configured
- Fixed chassisout.wav playing at startup on a saber powered on with the chassis already removed. The range backend was reporting its "chassis in" default before the first BladeID scan returned, so the real state arriving a moment later counted as a change. It now stays silent until it has an actual reading. The detect-pin method never had this, because it reads the pin during startup
- Added a compile error for BLADE_DETECT_PIN together with NO_BLADE_ID_RANGE when the chassis range is in use. Both add the same no-blade marker to the reading independently, so a blade-out value arrives doubled and chassis detect can never see the chassis as out. A detect pin already supplies that marker, so NO_BLADE_ID_RANGE should be removed in that combination
- No configuration change needed. JMT_CONFIG_STABLE_COUNT 1 is no longer required as a workaround and can be removed

Block swing-on ignition when no blade is installed
- New define JMT_SWING_ON_BLOCK swallows the swing-on gesture while the hilt is empty, so a swing cannot ignite a blade that is not there
- Works with either blade detect method: the standard BLADE_DETECT_PIN or the BladeID-driven JMT_BLADE_DETECT. Requires one of them
- Blade presence is read at the moment of the swing rather than from a latched flag, so a saber powered on with no blade already in is covered. Neither detect method turns gestures off at startup, which is the case this closes
- Only the swing-on gesture is affected. Button ignition, twist, stab and thrust on are untouched, and so are the swing events that combine with a button
- Optional. It has an effect alongside FETT263_SWING_ON or FETT263_SWING_ON_PREON, and is harmless without them
- The no-blade check now recognises both the standard ProffieOS NO_BLADE entry and a custom JMT_NO_BLADE_VALUE sentinel, instead of only one or the other
- JMT_BLADE_DETECT now fails to compile unless NO_BLADE_ID_RANGE or JMT_NO_BLADE_VALUE is also defined. Without a detect pin nothing pushes the BladeID reading into the no-blade bucket, so the no-blade entry in your blades array can never be selected and the feature silently never fires. On ProffieOS 8.0 or later set NO_BLADE_ID_RANGE around your measured blade-out reading; on 7.x use JMT_NO_BLADE_VALUE

Charge complete can now be set in volts, and no longer announces early
- The full check was expressed as a percentage. ProffieOS derives battery percent from voltage with a maximum of 4.1 V and clamps the result to 100, so every cell at or above 4.1 V reports exactly 100%
- A Li-ion reaches 4.1 V early in its constant-voltage phase with real capacity still to take, so charge complete could announce well before the charger finished. Seen on a cell sitting at 4.18 V and still charging
- Converted back to volts, the entire usable range of CHARGE_FULL_ENTER spans about 2 mV: 32700 is 4.0978 V and the maximum 32768 is 4.1000 V. No value of that define could reach the real end of a charge, and tuning it only moved the trigger by less than the noise in the reading
- Charge full can now be expressed directly in volts with CHARGE_FULL_ENTER_V and CHARGE_FULL_EXIT_V (defaults 4.15 and 4.05). Define either one and the state machine compares battery voltage instead; the percent defines are then ignored
- Set the enter threshold BELOW whatever your charge board actually floats at, or it can never be reached and full is never announced. Watch the serial monitor through a complete cycle and take the peak reading
- Existing configs are unaffected. Without the new defines the percent path behaves exactly as before

Charge audio no longer stutters while the charge preset is held
- While charging, the wrapper was checking the preset count on every pass of the main loop. That check is not free: it locks and remounts the SD card, and while the card is locked ProffieOS throws away any pending audio buffer refill instead of delaying it
- The result was starved playback during charging: chargebegin, battery level and charge complete could stutter, restart or drag
- The charge preset index is now remembered, so holding the charge preset costs no SD access at all. It is recomputed whenever charging ends or the preset moves, so a blade config change cannot leave a stale value behind
- No configuration change and no new options

Prop is now a single-file drop-in
- The prop no longer includes common/charge_state.h. That header only declares the charge-full flag, and the prop defines the flag itself, so the include never did anything
- common/charge_state.h is still needed by configs that use a charge-state style, which pull it in through functions/charge_full_prop.h
- No behavior change: this removes a redundant include and nothing else

Fix boot-loop from a noisy BladeID reading (chassis out)
- With the chassis out, an unstable open-circuit reading could dip past the no-blade threshold and make ProffieOS reload the font every scan, looking like the saber repeatedly starting to boot
- The wrapper now holds the current blade config until a different one reads steadily for several scans, so a transient dip no longer triggers a reload; a real blade insert/removal still registers
- Hold strength is tunable with JMT_CONFIG_STABLE_COUNT (default 3; set to 1 to disable)

Charge mode holds steady against BladeID activity
- While charging, the BladeID scan can no longer flip chassis-in/out or blade-in/out, so charge mode stops reacting to detection churn (no stray sounds, gestures, or preset reloads)
- A manual 'scanid' during charge no longer drops you out of the charge preset; it self-corrects
- Preset-change gestures are ignored while charging

More reliable chassis detect via BladeID range
- Chassis-out detection now debounces the BladeID reading instead of reacting to a single noisy scan, so open-circuit drift and the contact sweep while seating the chassis no longer flip chassis state back and forth
- Debounce strength is tunable with JMT_CHASSIS_RANGE_STABLE_COUNT (default 3 scans)
- New JMT_DEBUG_CHASSIS_RANGE option prints the raw reading each scan to help tune your ranges

Internal versioning workflow update
- Addons-repo versioning rules now match the JMT Studio pattern (explicit PATCH/MINOR/MAJOR bumps with defined criteria)
- Manifest schema adds an optional 'minStudioVersion' field for future Studio-coordinated MAJOR bumps
- No user-visible behavior change from v1.0.18

Added 'What's New' release notes
- This section. Now you can see what changed in the JMT Add-ons each time you update.
- No functional code changes from v1.0.17.

Added Pixel Relay style
- Alternating two-color flash on 1 or 2 pixels (red 9x then green 5x, etc.)
- Designed for Luke ROTJ cave-scene arrow accents
- Configurable: flash period, single-pixel mode, start-index offset
- Available as PixelRelay (top-level) or PixelRelayL (layer form)

Added chassis detect via BladeID resistance
- Detect chassis presence using the BladeID resistance reading instead of a dedicated detect pin
- Drop-in alternative to CHASSIS_DETECT_PIN, fires the same chassisin/out sounds and triggers
- Configured via JMT_CHASSIS_DETECT_RANGE (min/max of the chassis-out detection window)
- Lets removable-chassis builds reuse the BladeID line and save a physical detect wire

Added JMT_NO_BLADE_VALUE for blade detect on ProffieOS 7.x
- Brings the OS 8+ NO_BLADE_ID_RANGE behavior to users still on ProffieOS 7.x
- Lets you use a custom sentinel ohm value to mark 'no blade' in your BladeConfig
- Fires EFFECT_BLADEIN and EFFECT_BLADEOUT correctly on state transitions
- Plays bladein.wav and bladeout.wav on insert/remove
